# Difference equations {#sec-difference}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}
How do we document change in time?


In an official chess tournament (probably true for no pro too), after a player move a piece, he/she will tap a clock and then write down the move they have.
In this, there is a long historical database of all the games that have been played.

What do you see when you read is a sequence of move, alternating each player.

This is an example of using discrete variable to document changes in time.
In step 1 you know the step of the system, in step 2, there is another change.

However, if you look at move 15 you probably has now idea of how the chess board looks after move 14.
This is the idea of a recurrence.

So what is a difference equation, in short it is a mathematical stuff that record the state of something using .
You have already seen that called .
You could define it implicity, that is state next = f(state now) (see also Markov chain).

A big step is trying to define, this only works for few (see below)

It is an equation so there is the defining it and there is the solving it.


## Formal {.unnumbered}
A difference quation is an application from N to R or anything where
u_n+1 = f(u_n). This is a recurrence

We could of course define as u_next = f(u_n, u_n-1...).
